prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1341; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the insured this morning after a sideswipe on a multi-lane road while changing lanes. The insured described the other vehicle drifting into their lane as they merged, and the insured is the named driver on the policy.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant, who is not represented by an attorney, and confirmed the account of the lane change and contact on the driver side. The claimant reports neck and upper back discomfort and was seen at an urgent care clinic the same day.

Entry 3: Reviewed the photos submitted by the insured. The damage to the rear quarter panel and side mirror lines up with the described impact, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is known from our records or the inspection.

Entry 4: Obtained statements from the other driver and a passenger in a nearby vehicle. Both confirm the accident happened as the claimant described, with the other car moving into the adjacent lane during the change.

Entry 5: Claimant's account has stayed consistent across each conversation so far. The claimant was unsure which seat position they occupied at the moment of impact, and I have noted that for follow-up without treating it as a concern about the claim.

Entry 6: Medical records show a back strain with a force and direction that fit the crash. The claimant had treatment for the same area about eighteen months ago, and that earlier condition is adding to the current complaints.

Entry 7: Treatment has followed a typical course of physical therapy and medication, with symptoms easing steadily as the claimant improved. The provider's notes indicate the pace of recovery is in line with similar soft tissue injuries.

Entry 8: Confirmed with underwriting that the policy was in force at the time of loss and that nothing in the file points to damage predating coverage. The coverage check is complete.

Entry 9: Claim reviewed and assessed as consistent across the vehicle, the scene evidence, and the medical picture. The file is ready for the next review step, with the prior back condition noted in the injury assessment.
